description:
📝 Notes
Mar 9, 2026
R&D daily sprint
Invited Amir Houieh Unbody io Noémi Biró Gabor Kerekes
Attachments R&D daily sprint 
Meeting records Transcript 
Summary
Financial updates and project progress were reviewed with a demonstration of a new AI-generated interactive components pipeline.Civil and Breed ProgressNoémi Biró updated the team on extensive work on Civil, including creating visual prototypes and deep-dive research for loss support. Progress was also made on the Breed project with a prototype pushed to GitHub and built by Gabor Kerekes.Software Factory AdvancementsGabor Kerekes reported successful progress on the software factory's sandboxing and demonstrated a new floating, always-on thought capture tool. They also demonstrated a native Mac OS overlay window prototype for a breathing exercise that could be immediately helpful.AI Component Pipeline SuccessThe team successfully implemented an entire pipeline for AI-generating fully interactive components and shipping them to the front end. They decided this experiment will be documented as a sharable demo and integrated into the Mycelium project.
Details
Meeting Start and Participant Well-being: The meeting began with general greetings and a check-in on the participants' well-being, where Amir Houieh shared that they are trying to manage anxiety through working and spending time with family, noting that work is helping them cope. Gabor Kerekes and Noémi Biró expressed understanding and noted that Amir Houieh has remained focused despite the circumstances (00:00:00).
Noémi Biró's Updates on Civil and Breed: Noémi Biró reported working extensively on Civil since Thursday to understand its modules and create visual prototypes, with plans for a detailed session later (00:03:45). They also mentioned updating Gabor Kerekes on Civil on Friday and building on a prototype they designed for Breed, the mushroom project, which was pushed to GitHub and subsequently built by Gabor Kerekes. Their research process for Civil involved using Google deep dives for clinical research on loss support, compiling findings into a document, and creating visualizations using Stitch (00:05:06).
Amir Houieh's Updates and Financial Status: Amir Houieh had minimal updates on their work progress from Friday but confirmed receiving funds from Melissa for the first February invoice. They expressed anxiety regarding the larger, first invoice, which has not yet been paid due to ongoing entity issues (00:06:18).
Gabor Kerekes's Software Factory and Sandboxing Progress: Gabor Kerekes reported that the software factory is progressing well, particularly with sandboxing, and they plan to implement a setup that requires even less agent oversight (00:06:18). Gabor Kerekes demonstrated a new floating, always-on capture tool that uses a shortcut to save thoughts directly into the mycelium for later processing through an enhancement pipeline (00:07:27).
Demonstration of the Breathing Prototype: Gabor Kerekes also demonstrated a native Mac OS overlay window prototype for a breathing exercise, which is a transparent window overlaying the screen with an animation. They decided to prototype this specific tool because they felt it could be immediately helpful for themself (00:09:51).
AI-Generated Interactive Components Pipeline: Gabor Kerekes was most excited to share the successful implementation of an entire pipeline for AI-generating interactive components and shipping them to the front end (00:11:23). This allows for the dynamic generation of code that can handle arbitrary complexity and is not limited by constraints like JSON rendering (00:13:39). The generated components are fully interactive and can potentially be wired up to backend functions, such as pulling data from a live database (00:15:51).
Discussion on AI-Generated Component Integration and Documentation: The team discussed the potential of Gabor Kerekes's new pipeline, noting that it could be used to design entire front-end pages and weave itself into existing code (00:19:08). Gabor Kerekes plans to tidy up and share this as a deployable demo with the Unison community, and the team agreed to start documenting the experiment, possibly as a blog post or a sharable demo. The expectation is that this will integrate easily into the Mycelium project (00:20:12).
Next Steps for Civil and Mycelium Projects: Amir Houieh outlined the immediate tasks for the team, including preparing for an update post on social media and determining the tasks for the current week. The focus for Civil this week is for Gabor Kerekes to focus on the analytic dashboard alongside Mycelium work, and for Amir Houieh and Noémi Biró to brainstorm and iterate on sketches for the first batch of module ideas, which are to be ready to show Melissa by Wednesday (00:23:21). Amir Houieh and Noémi Biró plan to have a brainstorming session today after the meeting (00:24:37).
Pending Tasks and Follow-up on Safety Regulations: Amir Houieh noted they still need to send Minha's invoice. Noémi Biró followed up on the safety regulation papers that Amir Houieh was meant to review, and Amir Houieh confirmed they had looked at two of the documents but needs to revisit them to refresh their memory and share their written thoughts (00:25:36).
Discussion on Noémi Biró's Role and Expectations: Before concluding their part of the meeting, Amir Houieh initiated a discussion with Noémi Biró about their role in the team, acknowledging that they organically joined and that they need to discuss commitment, expectations, and skill sets to better define their collaboration. They decided to switch the call to a separate session for this discussion (00:26:45).
Suggested next steps
Amir Houieh will call Gabor Kerekes later this afternoon.
Amir Houieh will share content with The group for feedback regarding an update post on social media (LinkedIn and 3X) about the launch, the pit, or the lab in general.
Noémi Biró will ping Amir Houieh again with the links to the safety regulation papers.
Amir Houieh will look at the safety regulation papers again after the meeting to refresh memory and share thoughts.
